messages:
alex: Heads-up: drift detected after the autoscaler tweak over the weekend. Terraform says prod nodepool desired=12 but the cluster only has 8 active GPU nodes (4 drained/cordoned). GitOps reconcile tried to reapply this morning and failed due to an OPA constraint. @maria any context?

maria: We rolled out the more-aggressive scale-down CA policy Saturday night. Looks like the change also introduced a label flip on the nodepool (gpu-type from "v1" -> "a100"). OPA policy `prod-nodepool-label-stable` blocks label mutations in prod, so gitops can't push the correction.

jamie: Can you paste the reconcile error from the deploy logs?

deploy-bot: reconcile-controller: apply failed for k8s/resources/nodepool/redwood-prod-gpu - admission webhook denied: opa constraint 'prod-nodepool-label-stable' violated: attempted mutation of label 'gpu-type' on nodepool/redwood-prod-gpu

kevin: To summarize: TF state still expects 12 nodes, autoscaler scaled down to 8. Normally CA would scale back up, but because labels changed and OPA blocks the fix, gitops keeps failing. Short-term options: revert the CA change, temporarily relax OPA, or use the internal driftsweep escape hatch. All have tradeoffs.

alex: Impact: several DL-serving jobs are being scheduled to fallback variants in us-west-2 due to fewer GPUs — increased latency and throttles. Ballpark hit: degraded throughput + potential $2-3k/week in both opportunity + extra cloud-side fallback costs if this persists. Need quick mitigation.

maria: Proposed play: run the one-off internal driftsweep (scripts/driftsweep/run.sh) in dry-run, verify plan, then run with --approve which will perform a reconcile with the temporary flag `allow_label_mutation=true` in gitops. This bypass is documented as an escape hatch but needs owner sign-off.

jamie: If we go that route: two safety steps — (1) run dry-run and post full plan, (2) create an immediate canary by patching a single nodepool replica in prod and let it reconcile, confirm workloads recover. Example patch command: ```kubectl patch nodepool redwood-prod-gpu -p '{"spec": {"labels": {"gpu-type": "a100"}}}' --type=merge```

kevin: I'll run the dry-run now and attach logs. If output is clean, I'll wait for thumbs from @alex and @maria before `--approve`. I'll also include the terraform plan snippet in the PR for audit.

maria: :thumbsup: run dry-run and post. If it passes I'll approve the real run. I'll open a follow-up ticket to relax the OPA rule for label-only flips originating from infra pipelines, and we should add a guard in the CA change rollout to avoid label drift.

ops-bot: INCIDENT CREATED: #INC-2026 - "prod gpu nodepool drift" assigned to kevin. Priority: P2. SLA: 4h.

alex: Thanks team. Kevin, drop the dry-run link and the plan here. Also add rollback steps in the incident ticket (how to re-cordon, revert CA config, and re-run tf apply). cc @eng-oncall

kevin: Dry-run started: `scripts/driftsweep/run.sh --target nodepool --dry-run --filter redwood-prod-gpu`. I'll post logs in 2-3m.
